clue.text: Frozen body? Turn up temperature

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, which is to come

explanation.surface: An instruction to warm up something frozen, perhaps a chilled body or a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a description rather than a dictionary synonym: the nucleus of this heavenly body is largely ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this celestial object is a ball of ice and dust, so it is fairly called a frozen body.

clue.text: Mix 'n' match decoration, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of decoration might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Picking colours that go together might be decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make things harmonise or go together, as with clothes or colours.

clue.text: Bird's bill penetrating gullet

indicators.note: penetrating means the word for bill goes inside the word for gullet

parts.note: a maw is the throat or gullet of an animal
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: A bird's beak piercing a throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like the bird's beak, but it is an account (AC).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Dirty little hospital nurses recording for broadcast news? No!

indicators.note: nurses means the jumbled letters plus the hospital letter hold the other piece inside
dirty suggests the letters of little are messed up into a new order
broadcast means scattered abroad, so the word for recording is scattered into a new order

parts.note: notating is setting down in writing, recording

explanation.surface: A grubby little hospital where nurses record broadcast news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' rearranges little to TELLIT; 'for broadcast' scatters NOTATING into NOTINGAT, which 'nurses' sits inside before the H. It is a biblical line (2 Samuel): keep the news from your enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the line from David's lament urges keeping bad tidings from enemies, i.e. don't spread it about.

clue.text: Chap is carrying iron to platform

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: carrying means the word is holds the symbol for iron within it

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is lugging an iron up onto a stage or platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform' looks like a physical stage, but it is the political sense: a party's stated programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a party's platform is its published declaration of policies and aims.

clue.text: For now, an expression of self-loathing?

explanation.surface: For the time being, someone voices hatred of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split as ME ANTI ME, it is someone declaring they are against themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: in the interim, while waiting; and read as 'me, anti-me', a person opposed to their own self.

clue.text: Missing, as was masseur reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a masseur's work is to knead muscles, so the masseur was kneaded

explanation.surface: A masseur has gone missing, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The masseur did the kneading rather than being kneaded, but the sound is what counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lacking or wanting is required, so it was called for.

clue.text: Thought one would snarl about dirty supporter

indicators.note: about means the first two pieces go around the word for dirty

parts.note: felt means thought, as in believed
low means base or dirty, as in a low trick
a raveller is one who ravels or tangles, and to snarl is to tangle

explanation.surface: Someone thought a fellow would growl at a grubby fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarl' looks like a growl but means tangle; 'about' wraps the thinking word and the tangler round the word for dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Politics: a sympathiser with a cause, especially communism, who is not a party member.

clue.text: Hospitals showing arrogance over adopting a security group

indicators.note: adopting means the reversed word takes the other letters inside it
over means the word for arrogance is turned around

parts.note: airs are pretensions or arrogance
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a security alliance

explanation.surface: Hospitals displaying haughtiness after taking on a defence alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses AIRS to SRIA, which then 'adopts' A + NATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plural of an establishment for treating convalescents or the chronically ill.

clue.text: Farmyard sound in so-so nursing home

indicators.note: nursing means the word for so-so holds the word for home

parts.note: OK means passable or so-so
in means at home

explanation.surface: A noise from the farmyard in an average care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing home' reads as a care home, but splits: 'nursing' is the container signal and 'home' is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Onomatopoeia: the grunt a pig makes, a typical farmyard noise.

clue.text: Big girl starts to test seesaw

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, a clothing label meaning big
Cilla is a girl's name, as in the singer Cilla Black

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the word test, here its first two

explanation.surface: A large girl tries out the seesaw in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big girl' looks like one description but splits into a clothing size label and a name; 'starts to' here takes two opening letters, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to seesaw is to swing back and forth, as a pendulum does.

clue.text: Crease new sheets

parts.note: a crease is a line, as on a face or fabric

explanation.surface: An instruction to put creases in freshly laundered bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Material: bed sheets are traditionally made of flax cloth, and bedding generally is called by that name.

clue.text: Dicky bird's covering for a swallow?

explanation.surface: A small child's word for a bird, describing feathers fit for a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a bird's down, put in the mouth, is what a swallow (the gulp, not the bird) would be. 'Dicky' as low-spirited is a stretch, but 'Dicky bird' makes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being dicky is feeling poorly or low, and the phrase means dejected; and a bird's soft feathers taken in for a gulp sit inside the mouth.

clue.text: Consistent supply prepared by Spooner?

indicators.note: the reference to Spooner means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: stock is a supply of goods
ready means prepared

explanation.surface: A dependable supply readied by Reverend Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: utterly firm and dependable, unwavering.

clue.text: A handle for jug, all in enamel

parts.note: jug is slang for prison, as is nick

indicators.note: all in means only the inner letters of the word enamel, losing its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Describing the handle of an enamel jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like part of the jug but is slang for a name, and 'jug' is slang for prison; 'all in' keeps only the inside of enamel.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a handle is an informal name or alias, a familiar substitute for one's real name.

clue.text: About to meet host, call for video equipment

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
MC is a master of ceremonies, a host
to call for something is to order it

explanation.surface: About to meet the host, someone asks for video gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a portable video camera with built-in recorder.

clue.text: Cooking fuel behind ring

parts.note: the stern is the rear or behind of a ship
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A camping stove's fuel sitting behind its burner ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a US brand of jellied alcohol sold in cans for chafing dishes and camp stoves.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand: this canned jellied alcohol is burned to heat food, a familiar American catering fuel.

clue.text: Bullfighter pulled a pole up

parts.note: tore is the past of tear, to pull hard

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for pole reads upwards

parts.note: a rod is a pole

explanation.surface: A bullfighter hauled a pole upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bullfighter, especially one on horseback, in Spanish tradition.

clue.text: Fruit in this is completely sliced by mum

indicators.note: sliced by means the word for mum cuts into the middle of the other word

parts.note: in toto is Latin for completely, so the word that follows in makes toto
ma is an informal word for mum

explanation.surface: Fruit being entirely sliced up by mother in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this is completely' is a riddle: 'this' is the Latin word that follows 'in' in the phrase meaning completely, so the solver must supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: this red salad item develops from a flower and bears seeds, so it is technically a berry.

clue.text: Mother comes in to sell axe

indicators.note: comes in means the word for mother is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
to hawk is to sell goods, often by calling out in the street
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum arrives wanting to sell an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light war hatchet of North American peoples, a kind of axe.

clue.text: Athlete's kit is striking — stores energy

indicators.note: stores means the word for striking keeps the energy symbol inside

parts.note: swats means is striking, hits
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An athlete's outfit is impressive and holds energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like eye-catching, but is the verb hit. The answer is US for tracksuit wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing: tracksuit tops and bottoms worn for training are called this in informal American usage.

clue.text: Made no progress? Perhaps he was forgotten

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged differently, here into a new phrase

explanation.surface: Someone who achieved nothing was soon forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of 'he was forgotten'; the surface ties the failure to being forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase describes effort that brings no advance at all, staying stuck despite trying.

clue.text: F1 driver turned up for tea

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the driver's name reads upwards

parts.note: Felipe Massa is a Brazilian Formula One driver

explanation.surface: A racing driver arrives in time for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrived, but reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a black tea from north-east India, named after its growing region.

clue.text: Fluffy dessert with fruit

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A light pudding served with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery: a light pudding of beaten cream or egg whites with fruit purée.

clue.text: In jeopardy, he will hold back a monster

indicators.note: back means the contained letters are read from right to left
will hold means the letters are contained in the words jeopardy and he run together

explanation.surface: A man in danger keeping a monster at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold back' reads as restrain, but splits: 'will hold' signals letters inside 'jeopardy, he', and 'back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth: the many-headed serpent slain by Heracles is a classic Greek monster.

clue.text: Posh boy back in Asian resort in part of Spain

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the rearranged word
resort read as re-sort means the letters of Asian are put in a new order
back means posh plus boy are read from right to left

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class, posh usage
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A well-off young man returns to an Asian holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the anagram signal (re-sort), making ANSIA; 'back' turns U + LAD into DALU, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: the southern region of the Iberian kingdom containing Seville and Granada.

clue.text: One buys tea that officer gulps

indicators.note: gulps means the word for officer swallows the word for tea

parts.note: a purser is a ship's officer in charge of accounts
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: A ship's officer downs his tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a buyer is one who acquires goods by paying for them.

clue.text: Like a drink? Gin perhaps?

explanation.surface: Someone offered a drink asks if gin is on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is like rum, the spirit; the second is the card game gin, one variety of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: resembling the cane spirit, and a family of card games of which gin is one example.
